newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl, coal miners agree coal subsidy compromise.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, coal miners agree coal subsidy compromise.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Germany's protesting coal miners union have agreed to a compromise on subsidies for the coal industry until the year 2005, Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said on Thursday.
Bohl said the federal government and Germany's two coal-producing states would offer higher subsidies in the next few years than Bonn had originally proposed.

Bonn, which is struggling to meet the criteria for Europe's single currency, sparked off miners' protests by announcing last week it wanted to slash annual coal subsidies from nine billion marks now to 3.8 billion ($2.2 billion) by 2005.
The miners' union said this would cut 50,000 of the 90,000 jobs in the industry, which produces coal at three times the world market price.
Protesting miners occupying the hub of Bonn's political centre withdrew to nearby Cologne on Wednesday but threatened to come back in force if they were not happy with the result of Thursday's talks.
